title: Peristaltic pressure behind the egg's middle makes the front blunt and rear pointed

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Peristaltic pressure behind the egg's middle makes the front blunt and rear pointed

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Peristaltic contraction of the oviduct applies greatest pressure behind the middle of the forming egg, making the anterior end broader and the posterior narrower; the resulting tapered form also favours movement down the oviduct blunt end first.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. XV: On the Shapes of Eggs, and of Certain Other Hollow Structures

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: from the nature and direction of motion of the peristaltic wave the pressure will be greatest somewhere behind the middle of the egg; in other words, the tube is converted for the time being into a more conical form, and the simple result follows that the anterior end of the egg becomes the broader and the posterior end the narrower.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter XV, “On the Shapes of Eggs, and of Certain Other Hollow Structures”; topic “Mechanical conformation of the egg”. Scope: birds' eggs

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch15-04: needs-new-data, resolvability 0.43

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The mechanism makes measurable temporal predictions, but the decisive physiological variables are absent from standard repositories. Existing morphology cannot distinguish peristaltic pressure from other developmental causes.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Synchronize in vivo oviduct pressure maps and peristaltic-wave direction with repeated imaging of the deformable egg, then test whether peak pressure lies posterior to mid-egg and predicts anterior broadening, posterior taper and blunt-end-first transport. Mismatched pressure location or transport orientation would refute the mechanism.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Public egg-shape datasets do not include spatial pressure during shell formation.

Direct oviduct imaging and manometry are specialized and invasive.

Final shape alone cannot localize the causal pressure maximum.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The mechanism specifies where peristaltic pressure peaks and which end of the egg is anterior. Comparative shape and oviduct dimensions are public, and they do not contain that pressure profile or the direction of the peristaltic wave. A shape model can be made consistent with the story, but confirming or refuting the stated pressure pattern requires physiological measurements that are not yet a dataset.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Record pressure along the oviduct during peristalsis and test whether the maximum lies behind the egg's midpoint, with the blunt end anterior. The pressure map would confirm the mechanism; a mid-egg or anterior pressure peak, or blunt-end-rearward travel as the usual case, would refute it. Inferring the pressure peak from the finished taper assumes the model under test.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Open egg archives record the finished shape, not the pressure distribution that is supposed to have formed it.

Using taper to infer a posterior pressure peak repeats the hypothesis.
